title: said
parentNote: One word today, learned whole: said. The ai in it says the short e in bed, which is a thing those two letters do in this word and almost nowhere else, so there is nothing to puzzle out — it is sed, and the quicker you say it for them the better. The slip to expect is sayed, and it is a good mistake: ai has meant the sound in rain since day 73 and your child is applying the rule properly. Today also changes what a story can be. Until now nobody in this course has been able to speak, because there was no word to hang speech on, so eighty-eight days of stories have been somebody telling you what happened. With you yesterday and said today, two people can talk to each other, and that means speech marks — which your child has never seen. Point at a pair and say: the words between these two little marks are the ones Meg says out loud. Then read Meg's lines in a Meg voice and the narrator's in yours. That one trick teaches the marks faster than any explaining.

activities.sentence: Meg said, "It is an owl!" and she did point up at it.

activities.title: Meg said it is an owl
activities.prompt: Two of us talk in this story. The words in the little marks are the ones we say out loud.
lines: Up in the big oak sat a dark lump.
Meg said, "It is an owl!" and she did point up at it.
I said, "It is not an owl. It is a crow!" and Meg did huff.
Meg said, "Owls are big and crows are not," and she did cross her arms.
So we did creep up to the oak to see.
The lump did not stir, and it did not make a peep.
I did chuck a nut up at it, and down it did drop.
It did land in the mud with a thud. It is not an owl. It is not a crow.
It is the red hat Dad did drop in the storm at sun up.
Meg said, "I did tell you it is big!" and I did grin at her.
We did run in, and Dad said, "You did get it back!" and he did pop it on.
